title: Which cases get sampled?
hook: Two equally frequent cases have unequal windows for being detected.

knows: arithmetic means, rates and simple plotted values
doesNotKnow: screening finds slow-growing tumors more often, making screen-found cancers look less deadly.

misconception: Treating length bias as valid without checking the stated model, denominators or causal assumptions.
objective: screening finds slow-growing tumors more often, making screen-found cancers look less deadly.
keyState: Both finite cases completed; their computed summaries retained.

claims.text: Two equally frequent toy conditions are detectable for 1 and 4 months. A uniform-time screen samples in proportion to detectable duration. What share of detected cases is long-duration?
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-length-bias/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Model tumor A detectable1month, B detectable4months; onset frequencies equal. A uniform-time screening sample is weighted1:4, 80%slow tumors. The stage is exposure-time weighting, not a medical recommendation.

claims.text: Uniform-time screening retains 80% long-duration cases, while sampling at onset retains 50%. The long detectable window offers four times as much opportunity for capture.

claims.text: Duration weighting changes which cases enter the observed group. This is a toy exposure model, not clinical evidence or a screening recommendation; comparing the groups’ later outcomes would need to address that selection.

claims.text: Equal onsets last 2 and 6 time units. Under duration-weighted sampling, what fraction is long-duration? The long-duration share is 6/(2+6)=75%.
